headline: A Gulf peace headline did what the Fed couldn't — Brent -7.5% knocked the inflation leg out of the trade, yet VIX stayed pinned at 19.4.
summary: The marginal news today was crude, not chips. Brent fell 7.5% to 108.81 and WTI 4.2% to 99.75, back under 100, with RBOB gasoline down 9.5% in a session and 9.5% on the month (z=-0.99, rolling over). The catalyst was Iran-Qatar diplomacy on ending the war, with OPEC+ leaving December output unchanged — a risk-premium deflation, not a demand signal. Oil/gold fell 4.5% but is still +16.5% on the month and 31.7% above its 200-day, so this is the first dent, not the unwind. The direct consequence: yesterday's objection to the bond rally is on hold. A 38bp one-month collapse in the 5-year (acc z=-2.56), 35bp in the 10-year and 33bp in the 10-year real yield looked indefensible against accelerating energy; today it got cover. The inflation composite improved to -27. The 5-year breakeven at 2.46, +10bp on the month and turning up, is now the stalest price on the board.

Energy equities are the stranded asset. XLE closed Friday +13.9% on the month, 20.5% above its 200-day at the 100th percentile of its 52-week range; XOP +13.6% and 20.3% extended; XOM and CVX both +15% on the month, 22-23% above their 200-days, both at the 100th percentile. None of those marks contain today's crude break. The same trade that cushioned Friday's semiconductor rout — XLE +1.9% on a day SOXX fell 8.2% — is now the one carrying the most unhedged extension on the board.

Risk appetite improved at the edges without repairing. Korea led the bounce: KOSPI +2.2% and +7.1% on the week after a -16.3% month (z=-2.29), on strong October chip exports; Shanghai +1.1%, Hang Seng +0.4%, Sensex +1.7% with acceleration z=2.13. The forced-liquidation tell also cooled — silver +1.9% and gold +0.3%, with gold/silver -1.5% off a z=1.9, 20.6%-extended reading. Software over semis is the live rotation: IGV/SMH +3.8% in a day, +14.2% on the month, z=2.07, acceleration 2.36. But the volatility complex refused to pay for it. VIX finished unchanged at 19.42 on a day oil collapsed and Asia rallied; VIX3M is 20.78 (+7.3%), the term structure 0.935 and turning up, SKEW 149.76. HYG/IEF is still -2.3% on the month at z=-1.69. High-beta/low-vol is -16.2% on the month at z=-2.57, growth/value sits at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range, QQQ/SPY at z=-2.37. The risk regime nudged to -17 from -20: a pause, not a turn.

Underneath, the plumbing is tightening and the periphery is still bleeding. The TGA has rebuilt to $1.0402tn, +11.1% on the month and the 97th percentile of the year, while the reverse repo facility is down to $4.375bn — the 4th percentile, no buffer left to absorb it. Liquidity scores -25. Brazil is the open wound: USD/BRL +1.0% today and +9.6% on the week to 5.437 (z=1.20, turning up), EWZ -23.8% in five sessions, Bovespa z=-2.05 with acceleration -1.98. That is happening under a softening dollar headline — DXY -0.3%, EUR +0.3%, USD/CNY -1.0% on the month at the 0th percentile of the year — which makes it idiosyncratic, not systemic, and tradeable as dispersion. And housing still gets nothing from the rally: the 30-year mortgage is 7.24%, +21bp on the month and +109bp YTD even as the 10-year fell 35bp.

good.text: The oil risk premium deflated: Brent -7.5% to 108.81, WTI -4.2% to 99.75, gasoline -9.5% with z=-0.99 and rolling over. That removes the strongest argument against the one-month duration rally and pulled the inflation composite up to -27.
Asia bid the AI complex back: KOSPI +2.2% and +7.1% on the week off a z=-2.29 washout, Shanghai +1.1%, Hang Seng +0.4%, Sensex +1.7% with acceleration z=2.13. Friday's rout did not compound offshore.
Hedge liquidation paused. Silver +1.9% and gold +0.3% after a week of being sold to meet margin; gold/silver -1.5% from a 20.6%-extended z=1.9 reading. The forced de-grossing signature is fading.
Breadth remains the one unambiguously bullish internal: RSP/SPY z=3.0 with acceleration 3.55, equal-weight +4.9% on the month at the 92nd percentile, financials +5.8% with acceleration 1.73.
The dollar is easing without a crisis bid: DXY -0.3%, EUR +0.3%, GBP +0.3%, USD/CNY -1.0% on the month at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range, USD/MXN -0.7%, USD/INR -0.3% at z=-1.52.

bad.text: Volatility would not come in on good news. VIX flat at 19.42 while oil fell and Asia rallied; VIX3M +7.3% to 20.78, term structure 0.935 and turning up, SKEW 149.76. Dealers are not selling this dip in protection.
Credit is still quietly refusing. HYG/IEF -2.3% on the month at z=-1.69 with HYG -0.2% and in a down trend — the junk bid is lagging the Treasury bid by a wide margin.

Liquidity is being withdrawn mechanically: TGA at $1.0402tn, +11.1% on the month and the 97th percentile, against an RRP of $4.375bn at the 4th percentile. There is nothing left to cushion the drain; liquidity composite -25.

Brazil is accelerating the wrong way: USD/BRL +1.0% today, +9.6% on the week to 5.437 (z=1.20, turning up), EWZ -23.8% in a week, Bovespa z=-2.05 with acceleration -1.98. Argentina -9.1% on the week, Turkey -12.6% on the month.
Risk appetite internals are still broken: high-beta/low-vol -16.2% on the month at z=-2.57, growth/value at the 0th percentile, MTUM -10.5% at z=-2.05, IPO -10.1%, ARKK -9.4%, QQQ/SPY z=-2.37.

Energy equities carry the extension that crude just lost: XLE 20.5% and XOP 20.3% above their 200-days at the 100th/99th percentile, XOM and CVX 22-23% extended and at 52-week highs — all marked before today's 7.5% Brent break.

trades.name: Fade the oil-equity extreme
trades.line: Short XOP: crude lost its war premium, energy equity hasn't
trades.expr: Short XOP outright, or short XOP vs long RSP/equal-weight at 1:1 notional; alternatively December XLE put spreads to cap tail risk around the 29 November OPEC+ meeting.
trades.thesis: Energy equity is priced for a geopolitical crude curve. The premium that drove WTI +73.7% YTD is being negotiated away in Doha while XLE sits 20.5% above its 200-day at the 100th percentile with one-month relative strength of +14.9% vs the S&P. Equities repriced a 24% three-month crude rally; they have not repriced the reversal.
trades.trigger: Brent -7.5% to 108.81 and WTI -4.2% to 99.75 today, gasoline -9.5% on the day and -9.5% on the month (z=-0.99, rolling over), while XOP's last mark is 20.3% above its 200-day and XOM/CVX both sit at the 100th percentile of the year.
trades.stop: Brent closes back above 118 or WTI above 106 (talks collapse / OPEC+ cuts on 29 Nov); or XOP relative strength vs S&P makes a new high.
trades.target: XOP back to its 200-day, roughly 17% lower; XLE giving back half of its +14.9% one-month relative gain.

trades.name: Short the 5-year breakeven
trades.line: Short 5y breakeven at 2.46 — the oil impulse just reversed
trades.expr: Long 5-year nominal Treasury (FV futures) versus short 5-year TIPS, duration-matched; retail proxy: short TIP against long IEF at equal duration.
trades.thesis: The 5-year breakeven at 2.46 is +10bp on the month and turning up, built almost entirely on the crude and gasoline impulse. Core CPI is -8bp YTD on the index and in a down trend. If the Gulf risk premium keeps deflating, breakevens carry the adjustment while nominal yields have already done 38bp of the work in the belly.
trades.trigger: Brent -7.5%, WTI -4.2%, gasoline -9.5% today with gasoline -9.5% on the month at z=-0.99; 10-year breakeven already -2bp on the month at 2.34 while the 5-year refuses to follow.
trades.stop: 5-year breakeven above 2.60, or Brent reclaiming 118 — either means the inflation impulse is supply-driven and intact.
trades.target: 5-year breakeven at 2.25-2.30, roughly 20bp of carry-adjusted gain.

trades.name: Software over semis
trades.line: Long IGV / short SMH: AI software beats AI hardware
trades.expr: Long IGV versus short SMH, dollar-neutral. Size for a 15% move in the ratio; roll monthly.
trades.thesis: The capex chain is de-rating while the application layer is not. SMH is -14.2% on the month and SOXX -17.1%, with SMH/SPY at z=-2.31 and rolling over; IGV is only -2.1% on the month and still 11.0% above its 200-day with relative strength turning up. If AI spending disappoints, the hardware vendors eat the earnings cut and the software buyers keep the margin.
trades.trigger: IGV/SMH +3.8% in a single session, +14.2% on the month, z=2.07 with acceleration 2.36 and turning up — yet still at only the 37th percentile of its 52-week range after a -32% YTD drawdown, so the mean-reversion room is large.
trades.stop: IGV/SMH back below 0.185, or SMH/SPY turning up with SOXX reclaiming its one-month loss.
trades.target: IGV/SMH at 0.23, roughly 15% on the pair.

trades.name: Mexico over Brazil
trades.line: Long EWW vs short EWZ: LatAm dispersion, not LatAm beta
trades.expr: Long EWW versus short EWZ, equal dollar notional. Optional overlay: long USD/BRL spot against short USD/MXN to isolate the currency leg.
trades.thesis: The dollar is softening broadly while Brazil funds alone. BRL is the only major EM currency accelerating against a falling DXY, and the equity market is confirming it. Mexico's index is making new ground with Mexican peso strength. This is a local funding/fiscal event, so express it as dispersion rather than cutting EM exposure wholesale.
trades.trigger: USD/BRL +1.0% today and +9.6% on the week to 5.437, z=1.20 and turning up; EWZ -23.8% in five sessions and Bovespa z=-2.05 with acceleration -1.98; versus Mexico IPC +8.7% on the month at z=1.87 and USD/MXN -0.7% today.
trades.stop: USD/BRL back below 5.10, or EWZ outperforming EWW by 8% from entry.
trades.target: 12% on the spread; EWZ back to its 52-week lows versus a flat EWW.

trades.name: Own the hedge the tape won't price
trades.line: Buy Dec SPY put spread: VIX 19.4 ignored a genuinely good day
trades.expr: Buy December SPY 5%-out put spreads financed by selling 12%-out strikes; or a December VIX 22/30 call spread for convexity on a term-structure inversion.
trades.thesis: Oil collapsed, Asia rallied 2%+ and the dollar fell, and index volatility did not decline at all. That is a market where protection is being accumulated, not sold. With liquidity being drained mechanically and the risk regime still at -17, the asymmetry favours owning a defined-risk hedge at the 34th percentile of the year's VIX range.
trades.trigger: VIX unchanged at 19.42 despite a broadly constructive session; VIX3M +7.3% to 20.78, VIX/VIX3M at 0.935 and turning up, SKEW 149.76; TGA +11.1% on the month to $1.0402tn at the 97th percentile with the RRP at $4.375bn (4th percentile).
trades.stop: VIX sustained below 16 with VIX/VIX3M back under 0.85 and HYG/IEF turning up — then the de-grossing is done and the hedge is dead money.
trades.target: VIX 28 / SPY 6% lower; take profit on the spread at 3x premium.

trades.name: Silver against gold
trades.line: Long silver vs gold: fade the ratio at z=1.9
trades.expr: Long silver futures versus short gold futures at equal dollar notional (roughly 5 silver contracts per 1 gold); ETF proxy long SLV versus short GLD.
trades.thesis: The gold/silver ratio's +12.7% one-month surge was a liquidation artefact — silver is the leveraged leg that gets dumped first when books are cut. With the ratio 20.6% above its 200-day at z=1.90 and silver 29.1% below its own, the snapback trade is in the industrial metal, not the monetary one.
trades.trigger: Silver +1.9% versus gold +0.3% today, and the ratio -1.5% from a z=1.90, 20.6%-extended reading with acceleration still at 1.15; copper/gold simultaneously at the 100th percentile of its 52-week range, signalling the industrial bid is intact.
trades.stop: Gold/silver above 84, or silver making a new 52-week low against a stable gold price.
trades.target: Gold/silver at 70 — roughly 10% on the pair.

trades.name: Healthcare leadership
trades.line: Long XLV: 100th-pctile leadership funded by earnings, not capex
trades.expr: Long XLV core position, with LLY as the high-beta satellite and IBB for the biotech leg; fund partly from an underweight in XLK.
trades.thesis: The one sector whose leadership is paid for by delivered earnings rather than AI narrative. XLV is at the 100th percentile of its 52-week range with z=2.31 and acceleration 1.90, and its relative strength versus the S&P has turned up. As capex-chain multiples compress, this is where the index-level money goes.
trades.trigger: XLV +9.8% on the month, +14.2% over three months, relative strength +10.8% vs the S&P and turning up; LLY +3.2% in a session, +22.5% on the month at the 100th percentile; IBB +16.7% over three months at the 99.6th percentile; UNH +10.9% on the month.
trades.stop: XLV relative strength versus the S&P rolls over, or XLV drops 8% (back toward its 200-day, currently 17.3% below).
trades.target: Another 8-10% absolute; relative strength extending toward +15% over three months.
